correctness.rationale: The unitary Fourier transform converts every affine action into an ℓ^r isometry; transitivity makes its orbit average exactly c1_S. The established sharp synthesis constant makes the averaged Fourier norm (1−δ) times the original. The finite-group representation permits averaging Clarkson (r>2) or the Ball–Carlen–Lieb/Ricard–Xu midpoint inequality (1<r<2), and Jensen then bounds the orbit-invariant residual. At r=2 Pythagoras is exact. The Z7 two-frequency and Z3 antisymmetric families independently exhibit deficits of orders t^r and t² with distances of order t; therefore both claimed exponents are optimal. The checker produces 5,600 random instances and 21 asymptotic checks but is not an infinite certificate.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating work explicitly asks how near-optimal sharp synthesis forces proximity to modulated indicators with specified norm/modulus dependence. This theorem answers for the full affine-transitive class, for all real exponents, with modulus-independent Fourier ℓ^r control and mathematically necessary exponent switch at r=2. This is a motivated qualitative-to-quantitative stability extension, rather than a parameter substitution or a small computational table.
